readme:
# Toxic Comment Classifier ### A deep learning NLP project for detecting toxic, abusive, and harmful online comments 💬 ![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Completed-brightgreen?style=flat-square) ![Domain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Domain-NLP%20%7C%20Text%20Classification-blue?style=flat-square) ![Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model-BiLSTM-orange?style=flat-square) ![Micro F1](https://img.shields.io/badge/Micro%20F1-0.7317-success?style=flat-square) ![Micro ROC AUC](https://img.shields.io/badge/Micro%20ROC--AUC-0.9871-success?style=flat-square)
--- ## Table of Contents - [Overview](#overview) - [Business Problem](#business-problem) - [Key Features](#key-features) - [Tech Stack](#tech-stack) - [Dataset Summary](#dataset-summary) - [Exploratory Data Analysis and Preprocessing](#exploratory-data-analysis-and-preprocessing) - [Modeling Workflow](#modeling-workflow) - [Model Architecture](#model-architecture) - [Model Performance](#model-performance) - [Dashboard](#dashboard) - [Screenshots and Visual Results](#screenshots-and-visual-results) - [Project Structure](#project-structure) - [Future Improvements](#future-improvements) --- ## Overview **Toxic Comment Classifier** is a Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing project that detects toxic behavior in comments using a **Bidirectional LSTM** neural network. The project classifies each comment into one or more toxicity categories: - `toxic` - `severe_toxic` - `obscene` - `threat` - `insult` - `identity_hate` The complete workflow is implemented in a single notebook: ```text Notebook/Toxic_comment_classifier.ipynb ``` The notebook includes: - Data loading and quality checks - Text preprocessing - Exploratory data analysis - Text vectorization - Bidirectional LSTM training - Per-label threshold calibration - Evaluation reports and visualizations - Custom comment prediction - Interactive notebook and Streamlit dashboards --- ## Business Problem Online platforms receive thousands or millions of comments every day. Manually reviewing all comments is slow, costly, and difficult to scale. Toxic language can reduce user trust, damage community quality, and create unsafe digital spaces. This project frames toxic comment detection as a **multilabel text classification problem**: ```text Input : User comment text Output : Toxicity probabilities for six labels ``` | Area | Impact | | --- | --- | | Social media moderation | Helps identify abusive or harmful comments | | Online communities | Supports healthier discussion spaces | | Content safety | Flags high-risk text for review | | User protection | Reduces exposure to harassment and hate speech | | Automation | Assists moderation teams with scalable filtering | --- ## Key Features | Feature | Description | | --- | --- | | 💬 Toxic Comment Detection | Classifies text into six toxicity categories | | 🧹 Text Preprocessing | Cleans URLs, special characters, casing, and extra spaces | | 📊 EDA Visuals | Includes label distribution, correlation heatmap, and comment length analysis | | 🧠 BiLSTM Modeling | Uses a Bidirectional LSTM for sequence-based text learning | | 🎯 Multilabel Prediction | Allows one comment to belong to multiple toxicity classes | | ⚖️ Threshold Calibration | Uses per-label thresholds to improve rare class detection | | 📈 Model Evaluation | Reports F1-score, ROC-AUC, confusion matrices, and per-label metrics | | 📊 Dashboard | Provides notebook and generated Streamlit dashboards for custom predictions | | ⭐ Portfolio Ready | Clean README, visual outputs, project structure, and reproducible workflow | --- ## Tech Stack
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3776AB?style=for-the-badge&logo=python&logoColor=white) ![Pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pandas-150458?style=for-the-badge&logo=pandas&logoColor=white) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-013243?style=for-the-badge&logo=numpy&logoColor=white) ![Scikit Learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Scikit--Learn-F7931E?style=for-the-badge&logo=scikitlearn&logoColor=white) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-FF6F00?style=for-the-badge&logo=tensorflow&logoColor=white) ![Keras](https://img.shields.io/badge/Keras-D00000?style=for-the-badge&logo=keras&logoColor=white) ![Jupyter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jupyter-F37626?style=for-the-badge&logo=jupyter&logoColor=white) ![Matplotlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matplotlib-11557C?style=for-the-badge) ![Seaborn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Seaborn-4C72B0?style=for-the-badge) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-FF4B4B?style=for-the-badge&logo=streamlit&logoColor=white)
--- ## Dataset Summary The project uses the **Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification** dataset. | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | Dataset | Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification | | Main file | `Jigsaw_Dataset/train.csv` | | Total training records | 159,571 | | Problem type | Multilabel text classification | | Input column | `comment_text` | | Output labels | 6 toxicity categories | ### Target Labels | Label | Positive Comments | Percentage | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `toxic` | 15,294 | 9.58% | | `obscene` | 8,449 | 5.29% | | `insult` | 7,877 | 4.94% | | `severe_toxic` | 1,595 | 1.00% | | `identity_hate` | 1,405 | 0.88% | | `threat` | 478 | 0.30% | The dataset is highly imbalanced. Common classes such as `toxic`, `obscene`, and `insult` have far more examples than rare classes such as `threat` and `identity_hate`. --- ## Exploratory Data Analysis and Preprocessing The EDA section studies the dataset from both text and label-distribution perspectives. ### Analysis Performed - Checked dataset shape and missing values - Analyzed positive label counts - Visualized class imbalance - Compared toxic and non-toxic comment frequency - Studied comment length distribution - Created label correlation heatmap - Inspected multilabel relationships between toxicity classes ### Text Preprocessing | Step | Description | | --- | --- | | Lowercasing | Converts all text to lowercase | | URL removal | Removes links and web references | | Character cleaning | Keeps useful text symbols and removes noisy characters | | Whitespace cleanup | Removes repeated spaces | | Vectorization preparation | Prepares clean text for Keras `TextVectorization` | ### Key EDA Insights | Area | Insight | | --- | --- | | Class imbalance | Rare labels such as `threat` have very few positive samples | | Multilabel nature | One comment can belong to more than one toxicity category | | Common labels | `toxic`, `obscene`, and `insult` appear most frequently | | Rare labels | `threat` and `identity_hate` are harder to detect reliably | | Thresholding | A single `0.50` threshold is not ideal for every label | --- ## Modeling Workflow ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Raw Comment Dataset] --> B[Data Quality Checks] B --> C[Text Preprocessing] C --> D[EDA and Visualization] D --> E[Train Validation Split] E --> F[TextVectorization] F --> G[Embedding Layer] G --> H[Bidirectional LSTM] H --> I[Sigmoid Multilabel Output] I --> J[Threshold Calibration] J --> K[Evaluation and Dashboard] ``` ### Notebook Pipeline The complete modeling workflow is implemented in: ```text Notebook/Toxic_comment_classifier.ipynb ``` #### Steps 1. Load the Jigsaw toxic comment dataset. 2. Perform data quality checks. 3. Clean and normalize comment text. 4. Explore label distribution and text length. 5. Split data into training and validation sets. 6. Adapt a Keras `TextVectorization` layer. 7. Build a Bidirectional LSTM neural network. 8. Train the model with binary cross-entropy loss. 9. Evaluate model probabilities on validation data. 10. Calibrate per-label thresholds using validation F1-score. 11. Generate evaluation plots and CSV reports. 12. Save the trained model. 13. Test custom comments. 14. Display notebook and Streamlit dashboards. --- ## Model Architecture The classifier uses a text sequence deep learning architecture. ```text Input Comment | v Text Cleaning | v TextVectorization | v Embedding Layer | v Bidirectional LSTM | v Dense Layers | v Sigmoid Output Layer | v Six Toxicity Probabilities ``` ### Architecture Configuration | Layer / Component | Configuration | | --- | --- | | Text vectorizer | Keras `TextVectorization` | | Maximum tokens | 50,000 | | Sequence length | 200 | | Embedding dimension | 128 | | Recurrent layer | Bidirectional LSTM | | LSTM units | 64 | | Output units | 6 | | Output activation | Sigmoid | | Loss function | Binary cross-entropy | | Optimizer | Adam | ### Threshold Calibration Instead of forcing every label to use the same `0.50` cutoff, the project computes validation-based thresholds for each label. | Label | Calibrated Threshold | | --- | ---: | | `toxic` | 0.3898 | | `severe_toxic` | 0.2564 | | `obscene` | 0.4488 | | `threat` | 0.0576 | | `insult` | 0.2745 | | `identity_hate` | 0.1642 | This is especially useful for rare labels such as `threat` and `identity_hate`. --- ## Model Performance ### Training Summary | Split | Records | | --- | ---: | | Total rows used | 159,571 | | Training rows | 127,656 | | Validation rows | 31,915 | ### Performance Summary | Metric | Score | | --- | ---: | | Micro F1 | 0.7317 | | Macro F1 | 0.5511 | | Micro ROC-AUC | 0.9871 | | Macro ROC-AUC | 0.9786 | ### Per-Label Classification Report | Label | Precision | Recall | F1-score | Support | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `toxic` | 0.8126 | 0.7958 | 0.8041 | 3,056 | | `severe_toxic` | 0.4412 | 0.6199 | 0.5155 | 321 | | `obscene` | 0.8503 | 0.7714 | 0.8089 | 1,715 | | `threat` | 0.1066 | 0.3514 | 0.1635 | 74 | | `insult` | 0.6633 | 0.8116 | 0.7300 | 1,614 | | `identity_hate` | 0.2336 | 0.3639 | 0.2846 | 294 | ### Result Interpretation - The model performs strongly on frequent classes such as `toxic`, `obscene`, and `insult`. - Rare labels have lower precision because they have fewer positive training examples. - `threat` is the most difficult label because it appears in only about `0.30%` of training comments. - Per-label threshold calibration improves recall for rare toxicity classes. - ROC-AUC scores show the model separates toxic and non-toxic patterns well at the probability level. --- ## Dashboard The project includes two dashboard options: | Dashboard | Description | | --- | --- | | Notebook dashboard | Uses `ipywidgets` inside the Jupyter notebook | | Streamlit dashboard | Generated automatically inside `.generated/` from the notebook | The dashboard allows the user to enter a custom comment and view: - Probability score for each toxicity label - Calibrated threshold for each label - Detected categories - Horizontal probability chart - Overall toxicity score --- ## Screenshots and Visual Results ### EDA: Label Distribution ![Label distribution](Results/plots/label_distribution.png) ### EDA: Label Correlation Heatmap ![Label correlation heatmap](Results/plots/label_correlation_heatmap.png) ### EDA: Comment Length Distribution ![Comment length distribution](Results/plots/comment_length_distribution.png) ### LSTM: Training Curves ![LSTM training history](Results/plots/lstm_training_history.png) ### Model Evaluation ![Model evaluation](Results/plots/model_evaluation.png) ### Confusion Matrices ![Confusion matrices](Results/plots/confusion_matrices.png) --- ## Project Structure ```text Toxic Comment Classifier/ |-- Jigsaw_Dataset/ | |-- train.csv | |-- test.csv | `-- test_labels.csv |-- Notebook/ | `-- Toxic_comment_classifier.ipynb |-- Results/ | `-- plots/ | |-- label_distribution.png | |-- label_correlation_heatmap.png | |-- comment_length_distribution.png | |-- lstm_training_history.png | |-- model_evaluation.png | `-- confusion_matrices.png |-- models/ | |-- toxic_bilstm.keras | `-- label_thresholds.json |-- reports/ | |-- lstm_metrics.json | |-- per_label_results.csv | `-- label_thresholds.csv |-- requirements.txt |-- .gitignore `-- README.md ``` --- ## Future Improvements - Fine-tune transformer models such as BERT, RoBERTa, or DistilBERT. - Improve rare-label detection for `threat` and `identity_hate`. - Add class weighting or focal loss for imbalance handling. - Deploy the model as a web application. ---
**Built with Python, TensorFlow, NLP, and Deep Learning**

🏏 IPL Ball-by-Ball Analytics Dashboard

Power BI Sports Analytics Project | IPL 2008-2025

📊 A professional IPL analytics dashboard that transforms ball-by-ball cricket data into match, batting, bowling, and player comparison insights.

--- ## 🌟 About Project The **IPL Ball-by-Ball Analytics Dashboard** is an interactive **Power BI** project built on IPL delivery-level data from **2008 to 2025**. It helps users explore scoring trends, wicket patterns, venue behavior, team strengths, batting impact, bowling efficiency, and player comparisons through clean visuals and dynamic filters. > 🎯 **Goal:** Turn raw ball-by-ball IPL data into a decision-ready sports analytics experience for fans, analysts, and cricket data storytellers. --- ## 📌 Project Highlights | Area | Description | |---|---| | 🏠 Overview | High-level IPL history, runs, wickets, teams, players, boundaries, and season trends | | 🏟 Match Analysis | Match-level scoring flow, innings comparison, wickets timeline, and phase-wise momentum | | 🏏 Batting Analysis | Player runs, strike rate, boundaries, matchup strength, and phase-wise batting performance | | 🎯 Bowling Analysis | Wickets, economy, dot balls, runs conceded, and bowling effectiveness by phase | | ⚔️ Player Comparison | Side-by-side batsman and bowler comparisons for performance benchmarking | --- ## 🧰 Technologies Used ![Power BI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Power%20BI-F2C811?style=for-the-badge&logo=powerbi&logoColor=black) ![Power Query](https://img.shields.io/badge/Power%20Query-217346?style=for-the-badge&logo=microsoft-excel&logoColor=white) ![DAX](https://img.shields.io/badge/DAX-0F6CBD?style=for-the-badge&logo=powerbi&logoColor=white) ![CSV](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSV%20Dataset-4CAF50?style=for-the-badge&logo=files&logoColor=white) ![Data Visualization](https://img.shields.io/badge/Data%20Visualization-FF6F00?style=for-the-badge) ![Sports Analytics](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sports%20Analytics-DC143C?style=for-the-badge) --- ## 📂 Dataset Information The dashboard uses ball-by-ball IPL data from **2008-2025**, including match metadata, team details, batter and bowler information, scoring events, extras, and dismissal details. | Column Group | Fields | |---|---| | 🗓 Match Info | Match ID, Season, Date, Venue, Innings, Ball Number | | 🏏 Batting Info | Batting Team, Striker, Non-Striker, Runs Off Bat | | 🎯 Bowling Info | Bowling Team, Bowler, Wicket Type, Player Dismissed | | ➕ Extras | Extras, Wides, No Balls, Byes, Leg Byes | --- ## 📊 Dashboard Pages ### 🏠 Overview Dashboard **Purpose:** Provide a high-level summary of IPL history and long-term tournament trends. | KPIs | Key Visuals | Insights | |---|---|---| | Total Matches, Total Runs, Total Wickets, Total Boundaries, Total Teams, Total Players | Season-wise runs trend, wickets trend, team performance, venue analysis, runs distribution, match statistics | Identify scoring evolution, compare teams, and analyze IPL growth over time | ### 🏟 Match Analysis Dashboard **Purpose:** Analyze match-level scoring patterns, innings momentum, and phase-wise performance. | Features | Key Visuals | Insights | |---|---|---| | Match filters, team filters, powerplay, middle overs, death overs | Over-wise runs, innings comparison, runs progression, match run distribution, wickets timeline | Understand acceleration, wicket impact, and high/low scoring phases | ### 🏏 Batting Analysis Dashboard **Purpose:** Evaluate batsman performance across seasons, teams, and match phases. | KPIs | Key Visuals | Comparison | |---|---|---| | Total Runs, Strike Rate, Boundaries, Fours, Sixes | Top run scorers, strike rate analysis, boundary analysis, runs against teams, phase-wise batting | Compare any two batsmen by runs, strike rate, boundaries, and consistency | ### 🎯 Bowling Analysis Dashboard **Purpose:** Measure bowling impact, control, and wicket-taking ability. | KPIs | Key Visuals | Comparison | |---|---|---| | Total Wickets, Economy Rate, Dot Ball %, Runs Conceded | Top wicket takers, economy analysis, dot ball analysis, wickets by phase, bowling by team | Compare any two bowlers by wickets, economy, dot ball %, and effectiveness | --- ## 🖼️ Dashboard Screenshots ### 🏠 Overview ![Overview Dashboard](Screenshots/OVERVIEW/Overview.png) | Team View | Team View | |---|---| | ![CSK against other teams](Screenshots/OVERVIEW/CSK%20against%20other%20Teams.png) | ![RCB against other teams](Screenshots/OVERVIEW/RCB%20against%20other%20teams.png) | ### 🏟 Match Wise Analysis | RCB vs GT | RCB vs PBKS | |---|---| | ![RCB vs GT](Screenshots/Match%20Wise%20Analysis/RCB%20vs%20GT.png) | ![RCB vs PBKS](Screenshots/Match%20Wise%20Analysis/RCB%20vs%20PBKS.png) | ### 🏏 Batting Analysis | Virat Kohli | Rohit Sharma | |---|---| | ![Virat Kohli](Screenshots/Batting%20Analysis/Virat%20Kohli.png) | ![Rohit Sharma](Screenshots/Batting%20Analysis/Rohit%20Sharma.png) | ### 🎯 Bowling Analysis | Jasprit Bumrah | Bhuvaneshwar Kumar | |---|---| | ![Bumrah](Screenshots/Bowling%20Analysis/Bumrah.png) | ![Bhuvaneshwar Kumar](Screenshots/Bowling%20Analysis/Bhuvaneshwar%20Kumar.png) | ### ⚔️ Player Performance Comparison | ABD vs Dhoni| Virat vs Dhoni | |---|---| | ![ABD vs Dhoni](Screenshots/Player%20Performance%20Comparision/ABD%20vs%20DHONI.png) | ![Virat vs Dhoni](Screenshots/Player%20Performance%20Comparision/Virat%20vs%20Dhoni.png) | --- ## ✨ Features - 🎛️ **Interactive Filters:** Slice data by season, team, venue, player, match, innings, and phase. - 🏆 **Team Performance Tracking:** Compare franchise performance across seasons and venues. - 📈 **Season Trend Analysis:** Understand how runs, wickets, and match patterns changed from 2008-2025. - ⚡ **Phase-Wise Insights:** Analyze powerplay, middle overs, and death overs separately. - 🏏 **Batsman Deep Dive:** Track runs, strike rate, boundaries, and matchup behavior. - 🎯 **Bowler Deep Dive:** Evaluate wickets, economy, dot ball percentage, and pressure performance. - ⚔️ **Player Comparison:** Compare key players side by side for smarter performance storytelling. --- ## 🧮 Important DAX Calculations ### 🏃 Total Runs ```DAX Total Runs = SUM('IPL Data'[runs_off_bat]) + SUM('IPL Data'[extras]) ``` ### 🏏 Batsman Runs ```DAX Batsman Runs = SUM('IPL Data'[runs_off_bat]) ``` ### ⚡ Strike Rate ```DAX Strike Rate = DIVIDE( [Batsman Runs], [Balls Faced] ) * 100 ``` ### 🎯 Bowler Wickets ```DAX Bowler Wickets = CALCULATE( COUNTROWS('IPL Data'), NOT(ISBLANK('IPL Data'[wicket_type])) ) ``` ### 🟢 Dot Ball % ```DAX Dot Ball % = DIVIDE( [Dot Balls], [Balls Bowled] ) * 100 ``` ### 💥 Boundary % ```DAX Boundary % = DIVIDE( [Boundary Runs], [Batsman Runs] ) * 100 ``` ### 🧭 Phase Classification ```DAX Phase = SWITCH( TRUE(), [Over Number] <= 6, "Powerplay", [Over Number] <= 15, "Middle Overs", "Death Overs" ) ``` --- ## 🔥 Key Business Insights - 📊 Analyze IPL scoring evolution across **2008-2025**. - 🏏 Identify top-performing batsmen by runs, strike rate, and boundary impact. - 🎯 Discover wicket-taking bowlers and economy leaders. - ⚡ Understand powerplay, middle-over, and death-over strategies. - 🏟️ Evaluate venue-wise scoring patterns and match behavior. - 🆚 Compare player performance across teams and seasons. - 🧠 Find team strengths, weaknesses, and pressure-phase performance. --- ## 🗂️ Folder Structure ```text IPL DASHBOARD/ │ ├── Dashboards/ │ └── IPL Analysis.pbix │ ├── Dataset/ │ ├── IPL_ball_by_ball_2025.csv │ └── IPL_ball_by_ball_2023.csv │ ├── Screenshots/ │ ├── Batting Analysis/ │ ├── Bowling Analysis/ │ ├── Match Wise Analysis/ │ ├── OVERVIEW/ │ ├── Player Performance Comparision/ │ └── OVERALL.pdf │ └── README.md ``` --- ## 🔮 Future Enhancements - 🧩 Add win probability and match momentum indicators. - 🏆 Include playoff, final, and title-winning trend analysis. - 📱 Optimize layouts for mobile dashboard viewing. --- ## 📬 Contact **Mahammad Irfan Shaik** - 📧 Email: [smdirfan182@gmail.com](mailto:smdirfan182@gmail.com) - 💼 LinkedIn: [mahammad-irfan-shaik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mahammad-irfan-shaik-579828286/) - 💻 GitHub: [IRFAN18727](https://github.com/IRFAN18727) ---

⭐ If you found this project useful, consider giving it a star!

Made with ❤️ using Power BI, DAX, and cricket data 🏏

readme:
# Weather Forecasting Bangalore ### A machine learning project for predicting next-day rainfall using historical Bangalore weather data ☔ ![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Completed-brightgreen?style=flat-square) ![Domain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Domain-Weather%20Forecasting-blue?style=flat-square) ![Best Accuracy](https://img.shields.io/badge/Best%20Accuracy-~86%25-success?style=flat-square)
--- ## Table of Contents - [Overview](#overview) - [Business Problem](#business-problem) - [Key Features](#key-features) - [Tech Stack](#tech-stack) - [Dataset](#dataset-summary) - [Exploratory Data Analysis](#exploratory-data-analysis) - [Modeling Workflow](#modeling-workflow) - [Model Performance](#model-performance) - [Screenshots and Visual Results](#screenshots-and-visual-results) - [Project Structure](#project-structure) --- ## Overview **Rain Forecasting Bangalore** is a machine learning project that predicts whether it will rain the next day in Bangalore using historical daily weather observations. The project combines: - Statistical and visual exploratory data analysis - Time-series weather pattern inspection - Feature engineering with lag and rolling-window variables - XGBoost classification for structured weather data - LSTM sequence modeling for temporal rainfall patterns - Model evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and training curves The final notebook results show that both **XGBoost** and **LSTM** models can reach approximately **85-86% accuracy**, with XGBoost offering stronger interpretability through feature importance and LSTM offering a sequence-based modeling approach. --- ## Business Problem Rain prediction is valuable for agriculture, transportation, event planning, city operations, and public safety. Even a simple next-day rainfall forecast can support better decision-making in areas such as: | Area | Impact | | --- | --- | | Agriculture | Helps farmers plan irrigation, pesticide use, and harvesting | | Urban planning | Supports drainage, flood preparedness, and traffic planning | | Public services | Helps prepare for weather-related disruptions | | Logistics | Improves delivery and transport scheduling | | Daily life | Helps individuals plan travel and outdoor activities | This project frames rainfall forecasting as a **binary classification problem**: ```text Input : Historical weather features Output : RainTomorrow = 0 or 1 ``` --- ## Key Features | Feature | Description | | --- | --- | | 🌦️ Weather Data Analysis | Studies daily Bangalore weather observations from 1981 to 2024 | | 📊 EDA Visuals | Includes time-series plots, target distribution, heatmaps, and decomposition analysis | | 🧩 Feature Engineering | Adds lag features and rolling statistics to capture historical weather behavior | | 🚀 XGBoost Modeling | Trains a high-performing gradient boosting classifier for tabular features | | 🧠 LSTM Modeling | Builds a stacked recurrent neural network for sequence-based rainfall prediction | | 📈 Model Evaluation | Compares models using classification reports, accuracy, confusion matrices, and training curves | | 💾 Saved Artifacts | Stores trained models for reuse and future deployment | | ⭐ Portfolio Documentation | Clean README structure, visuals, badges, workflow, and results | --- ## Tech Stack
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3776AB?style=for-the-badge&logo=python&logoColor=white) ![Pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pandas-150458?style=for-the-badge&logo=pandas&logoColor=white) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-013243?style=for-the-badge&logo=numpy&logoColor=white) ![Scikit Learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Scikit--Learn-F7931E?style=for-the-badge&logo=scikitlearn&logoColor=white) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-FF6F00?style=for-the-badge&logo=tensorflow&logoColor=white) ![Jupyter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jupyter-F37626?style=for-the-badge&logo=jupyter&logoColor=white) ![Matplotlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matplotlib-11557C?style=for-the-badge) ![Seaborn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Seaborn-4C72B0?style=for-the-badge) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-FF6600?style=for-the-badge)
--- ### Dataset Summary | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | Location | Bangalore | | Time range | 1981 to 2024 | | Total records | 15,706 | | Prediction target | `RainTomorrow` | | Problem type | Binary classification | | Rain tomorrow count | 9,720 | | No rain tomorrow count | 5,986 | ### Target Classes | Class | Meaning | Count | | --- | --- | ---: | | `0` | No rain tomorrow | 5,986 | | `1` | Rain tomorrow | 9,720 | The dataset is moderately imbalanced toward rainy days. Because of this, the project evaluates **precision**, **recall**, and **F1-score** along with accuracy. ### Main Features | Feature Group | Columns | | --- | --- | | Date | `YEAR`, `MO`, `DY` | | Temperature | `T2M`, `TS`, `T2M_RANGE`, `T2M_MAX`, `T2M_MIN` | | Rainfall | `PRECTOTCORR`, `RainToday`, `RainTomorrow` | | Humidity | `RH2M`, `QV2M` | | Pressure | `PS` | | Wind speed | `WS2M`, `WS10M`, `WS50M` | | Wind direction | `WD10M`, `WD50M` | --- ## Exploratory Data Analysis The EDA notebook explores the dataset from statistical, visual, and time-series perspectives. ### Analysis Performed - Checked weather variables across the full historical date range - Visualized temperature, precipitation, and humidity trends - Studied rainfall class distribution - Created a correlation heatmap for numerical weather features - Inspected monthly weather behavior for selected periods - Applied seasonal decomposition on precipitation - Used STL decomposition to separate trend, seasonality, and residual behavior - Checked precipitation autocorrelation for time dependency ### Key EDA Insights | Area | Insight | | --- | --- | | Target distribution | Rainy days are more frequent than non-rainy days | | Humidity | Humidity-related variables are important rainfall indicators | | Rain history | `RainToday` is a useful signal for predicting `RainTomorrow` | | Time dependency | Lag and rolling features help represent recent weather behavior | | Model choice | Both tabular and sequence-based models are suitable for experimentation | --- ## Modeling Workflow ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Raw Weather Dataset] --> B[Data Cleaning and Exploration] B --> C[EDA and Visualization] C --> D[Feature Engineering] D --> E[Chronological Train Validation Test Split] E --> F[XGBoost Model] E --> G[LSTM Model] F --> H[Evaluation Metrics] G --> H H --> I[Saved Model Artifacts] ``` ### XGBoost Pipeline The XGBoost workflow is implemented in: ```text Notebooks/xgboost RainForecast.ipynb ``` #### Steps 1. Load the dataset. 2. Analyze target distribution and correlations. 3. Select weather-based predictor variables. 4. Create lag features for important variables: - `RainToday` - `QV2M` - `RH2M` - `WD50M` - `WD10M` 5. Create rolling mean and rolling standard deviation features. 6. Split the data chronologically into train, validation, and test sets. 7. Scale features using `RobustScaler`. 8. Train an `XGBClassifier`. 9. Evaluate using classification report, confusion matrix, feature importance, and log-loss curves. 10. Save the trained model to `Models/xgb_model.pkl`. #### XGBoost Configuration | Parameter | Value | | --- | --- | | `n_estimators` | 200 | | `max_depth` | 8 | | `learning_rate` | 0.1 | | `subsample` | 0.8 | | `colsample_bytree` | 0.8 | | `random_state` | 42 | ### LSTM Pipeline The main LSTM workflow is implemented in: ```text Notebooks/LSTMRain.ipynb ``` #### Steps 1. Load the weather dataset. 2. Identify features correlated with `RainTomorrow`. 3. Select sequence-focused features: - `RainToday` - `QV2M` - `RH2M` - `WD50M` - `WD10M` - `T2M_MIN` 4. Split data chronologically to avoid future leakage. 5. Scale features using `MinMaxScaler`. 6. Convert labels to categorical format. 7. Compute class weights for imbalance handling. 8. Create sequences with a sequence length of `7`. 9. Experiment with seasonal sequence generation using a `90`-day seasonal cycle. 10. Train a stacked LSTM model. 11. Evaluate the model using classification metrics and visual plots. 12. Save trained LSTM model artifacts. #### LSTM Architecture | Layer | Configuration | | --- | --- | | LSTM | 128 units, returns sequences | | Dropout | 0.3 | | LSTM | 64 units | | Dropout | 0.3 | | Dense | 32 units, ReLU activation | | Output | 2 units, sigmoid activation | --- ## Model Performance ### Performance Summary | Model | Approach | Reported Accuracy | Notes | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | XGBoost | Tabular model with lag and rolling features | ~86% | Strong accuracy and interpretable feature importance | | LSTM | Sequence model with class weighting | ~85-86% | Captures temporal weather patterns | | LSTM experiment | Additional class-weighted sequence experiment | ~82% | Useful for comparing imbalance strategies | ### XGBoost Classification Report | Class | Precision | Recall | F1-score | Support | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | No rain | 0.86 | 0.79 | 0.82 | 1,245 | | Rain | 0.87 | 0.92 | 0.89 | 1,885 | | Weighted average | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.86 | 3,130 | ### LSTM Classification Report | Class | Precision | Recall | F1-score | Support | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | No rain | 0.85 | 0.79 | 0.82 | 1,031 | | Rain | 0.87 | 0.91 | 0.89 | 1,571 | | Weighted average | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.86 | 2,602 | ### Result Interpretation - XGBoost and LSTM both achieve strong performance near **86% accuracy**. - XGBoost performs well on engineered tabular features and is easier to interpret. - LSTM is useful for learning temporal dependencies and experimenting with seasonal sequences. - Both models show stronger recall for rainy days than non-rainy days. - Since the dataset is imbalanced, F1-score and recall are more informative than accuracy alone. --- ## Screenshots and Visual Results ### EDA: Weather Time-Series Trends ![Weather time-series trends](Results/plots/eda_time_series_weather.png) ### EDA: Correlation Heatmap ![Correlation heatmap](Results/plots/eda_correlation_heatmap.png) ### EDA: RainTomorrow Distribution ![RainTomorrow distribution](Results/plots/eda_rain_tomorrow_distribution.png) ### XGBoost: Confusion Matrix ![XGBoost confusion matrix](Results/plots/xgboost_confusion_matrix.png) ### XGBoost: Feature Importance ![XGBoost feature importance](Results/plots/xgboost_feature_importance.png) ### XGBoost: Training and Validation Log Loss ![XGBoost log-loss curve](Results/plots/xgboost_logloss_curve.png) ### LSTM: Training Curves ![LSTM training curves](Results/plots/lstm_training_curves.png) ### LSTM: Confusion Matrix ![LSTM confusion matrix](Results/plots/lstm_confusion_matrix.png) --- ## Project Structure ```text Rain Forecasting Banglore/ |-- Data/ | `-- BangloreDATA.csv |-- Models/ | |-- lstm_model.pkl | |-- lstm_model2.pkl | `-- xgb_model.pkl |-- Notebooks/ | |-- EDA_RainDATA.ipynb | |-- LSTMRain.ipynb | |-- LSTMRain_without_test .ipynb | `-- xgboost RainForecast.ipynb |-- Results/ | `-- plots/ | |-- eda_time_series_weather.png | |-- eda_correlation_heatmap.png | |-- eda_rain_tomorrow_distribution.png | |-- xgboost_confusion_matrix.png | |-- xgboost_feature_importance.png | |-- xgboost_logloss_curve.png | |-- lstm_training_curves.png | `-- lstm_confusion_matrix.png |-- requirements.txt |-- test.py |-- gitignore.txt `-- README.md ``` ---

# Smart Security Camera using Computer Vision

---

## Project Overview

This project implements a Smart Security Camera system using Computer Vision to automatically detect persons, identify faces, and alert users in real time through Telegram.

The system uses Machine Learning models for object detection and face recognition to monitor environments such as homes, offices, or public areas — without requiring manual monitoring.

---

## Problem Statement

Traditional CCTV systems only record footage and require manual monitoring.
This project builds an intelligent surveillance system that can:

- Detect humans automatically using deep learning
- Recognize known and unknown faces
- Track multiple persons simultaneously with independent timers
- Alert users instantly via Telegram with captured images
- Log every detection event with entry time, exit time and duration
- Reduce the need for manual camera monitoring completely

---

## Features

- Real-time person detection using YOLOv8
- Multi-object tracking with unique ID per person (ByteTrack)
- Face recognition — known vs unknown identification (DeepFace)
- Independent parallel timer per person in frame
- Every person captured — clarity face image with entry/exit/duration info
- 30 second alert — sound + 2 Telegram images (full frame + clarity face)
- SQLite database logging for all detections and alerts
- Live Streamlit dashboard with charts, stats and image gallery
- Docker support for containerized deployment

---

## Tech Stack

**Programming Language:**
- Python 3.11

**Machine Learning & Computer Vision:**
- YOLOv8n (Ultralytics) — real-time person detection
- DeepFace + Facenet — face recognition
- OpenCV — video processing, face detection, image enhancement
- ByteTrack — multi-object tracking

**Backend & Database:**
- SQLite — detection and event logging
- Loguru — structured logging with daily rotation

**Dashboard & Visualization:**
- Streamlit — live monitoring dashboard
- Plotly — interactive charts

**Alert System:**
- Telegram Bot API — instant photo alerts

**DevOps:**
- Docker — containerized deployment
- python-dotenv — secure secrets management

**Tools:**
- VS Code
- GitHub
- Docker Desktop

---

## Project Structure

```
Smart-Security-Camera/
│
├── src/
│   ├── detector.py           # YOLOv8 detection + ByteTrack tracking
│   ├── timer_manager.py      # Parallel independent timers per person
│   ├── capture.py            # Best face scoring + image enhancement
│   ├── face_recognizer.py    # DeepFace Facenet recognition
│   ├── alert.py              # Telegram alert dispatcher
│   ├── database.py           # SQLite event logging
│   └── logger_config.py      # Loguru setup
│
├── known_faces/              # Register known persons here
│
├── main.py                   # Entry point
├── dashboard.py              # Streamlit live dashboard
├── config.py                 # All settings and constants
│
├── Dockerfile                # Docker image definition
├── docker-compose.yml        # Multi-service orchestration
├── requirements.txt          # Python dependencies
├── .env.example              # Environment variable template
└── README.md
```

---

## Machine Learning Models

### Person Detection — YOLOv8n
- COCO-pretrained model detecting persons in real time
- Achieves 20+ FPS on CPU
- Confidence threshold configurable in `config.py`

### Multi-Object Tracking — ByteTrack
- Assigns unique persistent ID to each person
- Handles occlusion and re-entry with grace period
- Each track ID gets independent timer

### Face Recognition — DeepFace + Facenet
- Facenet model for fast and accurate recognition
- Haar Cascade + eye detection for best face quality scoring
- Laplacian sharpness × face area × eye bonus scoring system
- Runs every 15 frames in background thread for performance

### Image Enhancement
- CLAHE contrast enhancement (LAB colorspace)
- Unsharp mask sharpening
- FastNlMeans denoising
- Applied to all alert images before sending

---


## How It Works

```
Webcam Feed
    ↓
YOLOv8n detects persons
    ↓
ByteTrack assigns unique ID per person
    ↓
Best face scored every frame (sharpness × area × eye bonus)
    ↓
DeepFace identifies known vs unknown (every 15 frames)
    ↓
Independent timer runs per person
    ↓
Person leaves < 30s  →  1 Telegram image (face + info overlay)
Person stays ≥ 30s   →  Sound alert + 2 Telegram images
    ↓
All events logged to SQLite
    ↓
Streamlit dashboard shows live stats
```

---

## Results

The system successfully:

- Detects and tracks multiple persons simultaneously with independent timers
- Recognizes registered faces with name and confidence score displayed live
- Captures clearest face (open eyes priority) throughout the entire visit
- Sends Telegram alerts within 1 second of trigger
- Logs every visit with accurate entry time, exit time and duration

**Telegram alert example:**
```
🔴 30s SECURITY ALERT
──────────────────────────
🚨 UNKNOWN PERSON
──────────────────────────
🕐 In time    : 14:32:10
🚪 Out time   : 14:33:05
⏱ Duration   : 55.2 seconds
🆔 Track ID   : 3
No match in database
```

---

## Future Improvements

- Multi-camera support with multiprocessing
- Cloud storage for captured images (AWS S3)
- Mobile app dashboard
- Night vision / low-light enhancement
- Raspberry Pi edge deployment with ONNX export
- Email alerts as fallback when Telegram fails
